target_customer: Landlords, listing agents and small property managers
problem: Landlords must post each unit on many listing sites and manage applications and screening by hand.
business_model: SaaS charged per managed listing (free during beta, per TechCrunch June 2012)
product_category: rental listing syndication and tenant application software

founders.name: Nikhil Abraham
founders.background_notes: The YC page bio describes ed-tech, D2C and healthcare roles with an exit to a public company; it may describe later career and is not tied to a dated employer.

competitors.name: YouGotListings
competitors.what: Broker tested rental listing management software

technical_complexity.rationale: Listing forms, syndication to portals, applications and e-signing are mostly integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Syndication depended on third party portals, and the product was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes an incumbent response; Rentobo itself posted to Craigslist, Zillow and Trulia.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (June 2012) described landlords filling units through many sites with messy paperwork; no spend or demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Exact .com rentobo.com per the YC page; no history found.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.visual_style: A blog post (via search summary) calls the design refreshingly beautiful.
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain: 'The easiest way to find a tenant.'

brand_strength.rationale: Little press or community evidence beyond one TechCrunch article.

pivots.to: Listing syndication and tenant applications for landlords
pivots.why: TechCrunch June 2012 says the team began by considering rental auctions; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Rentobo moved from an auction idea to one tool for posting rental listings and collecting applications, was still in free beta in June 2012, and is inactive today. No funding amount, exit details or shutdown reason was found, so its fate is not public.
notes: rentobo.com did not resolve from this session, so the site is treated as dead or blocked. Seedtable gives a last funding date of 2011-06-01 with no amount and paywalled investors; this rests on one database and is recorded with stage other. Dealroom labels the company Acquired with no acquirer or date, which conflicts with YC inactive and is unverified. The TechCrunch 2012 article does not name founders; the four names come from the YC page.
